name: Pakora
description: Crispy Pakistani vegetable pakoras with thin potato and onion coated in a seasoned besan batter, fried in controlled heat until crisp outside and cooked through.
ingredients: ¾ tsp red chili powder, optional
method: Combine the gram flour, cumin, ajwain, red chilli and salt. Whisk in water gradually until you have a thick batter that clings to the vegetables instead of running straight off them.
Add the thin potato slices, onion, green chillies and coriander and mix thoroughly. Let the mixture stand only briefly while the frying oil heats; onions may release moisture as they sit.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Test with a small amount of batter: it should rise and bubble steadily rather than darkening almost immediately or sinking without activity.
Drop small portions into the oil with space between them. Fry in manageable batches so adding too much cold batter does not sharply reduce the oil temperature.

Turn as needed and cook until deeply golden and crisp, checking that the potato inside is tender. If the outside browns much earlier than the centre cooks, reduce the heat slightly for the next batch.
Drain the pakoras on a rack or absorbent paper without piling them tightly while steaming hot, then serve promptly with chutney.
tips: Slice potatoes thinly so they cook through before the batter becomes too dark.
If the batter becomes watery after the onions release moisture, mix in a little more gram flour.
Avoid excessively hot oil, which can brown the outside while leaving the centre undercooked.
storage: Pakoras are best freshly fried. Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat with dry heat until thoroughly hot and crisp.
image_alt: Crispy Pakistani potato onion pakoras in seasoned besan batter with green chilli and coriander
image_caption: Potato and onion pakoras fried in controlled heat until crisp outside and fully cooked inside.
technique: Pakora batter should cling thickly to the vegetables. Onion releases water after mixing, so judge batter consistency again just before frying and add a little besan if it has loosened. Maintain medium frying heat so thin potato slices cook before the coating becomes too dark.
doneness_cues: Batter should coat vegetables rather than drip away in a thin stream.
A test drop should rise and bubble steadily without blackening quickly.
Potato inside a finished pakora should be tender.
Exterior should stay crisp after a brief drain rather than feel oil-soaked.
mistakes: Using thick potato slices that remain raw inside.
Crowding the fryer and dropping oil temperature sharply.
Frying in excessively hot oil that darkens besan before vegetables cook.
Piling steaming-hot pakoras into a covered bowl.
substitutions: Other quick-cooking vegetables can be used if cut to a suitable size.
Ajwain can be reduced for a milder aroma.
If onions make the batter watery, correct with besan rather than more spice.
reheating: Use an oven, air fryer or dry pan until thoroughly hot and crisp; microwaving usually softens the coating.
serving: Serve immediately with green chutney or tamarind chutney.

faqs.question: Why are pakoras oily?
faqs.answer: Oil may be too cool or the pan overcrowded. Fry manageable batches at steady medium heat.

faqs.question: Why are potato pakoras raw inside?
faqs.answer: Potato slices are likely too thick or the oil too hot. Slice thinly and let the centre cook before deep browning.

faqs.question: Why did the batter become thin while waiting?
faqs.answer: Salt draws moisture from onions and vegetables. Recheck consistency immediately before frying.
